title: Paver Driveway Cost in the East Bay: 2026 Pricing Guide
metaTitle: Paver Driveway Cost in East Bay 2026 | Real Lamorinda Numbers
excerpt: What does a paver driveway actually cost in Lafayette, Moraga, Orinda, and the broader East Bay in 2026? Real installed numbers from 100+ projects, broken down by size, pattern, and site conditions.
secondaryKeywords: paver driveway cost per square foot bay area
geoFocus: East Bay (Lafayette, Moraga, Orinda, Walnut Creek + surrounding Contra Costa)

outline.notes: 2-4 sentence direct answer. Lead with the typical East Bay range — something like '$18 to $32 per installed square foot, with most Lafayette and Orinda projects landing $20K-$45K'. Anchor the rest of the post.

outline.h2: What drives the price of a paver driveway in the East Bay
h3: Paver type and pattern (herringbone, running bond, modular blends)
Base preparation depth (and why East Bay clay soil matters)
Demo and disposal of existing concrete or asphalt
outline.notes: Each subsection 2-3 paragraphs. Hit clay soil specifically — Lafayette/Orinda/Moraga sit on expansive clays that require deeper base prep than the manufacturer minimum.

outline.h2: 2026 paver driveway cost ranges by project size
outline.notes: Table with 3 size tiers: small (under 600 sq ft), mid (600-1200 sq ft), large (1200+ sq ft). Include cost range, typical timeline, common scope. Make it a real markdown table.

outline.h2: Paver vs concrete: the 20-year cost comparison
outline.notes: Comparison table covering upfront cost, lifespan, maintenance, repairability. Pavers more upfront, but interlocking pavers don't crack with ground movement (key for clay-soil East Bay). Real numbers.

outline.h2: What a paver driveway project looks like in Lafayette vs Orinda vs Walnut Creek
h3: Lafayette: hillside lots, drainage as the hidden cost driver
Orinda: longer driveways, often with circular or motor-court layouts
Walnut Creek: flatter lots, faster installs, smaller cost variance
outline.notes: Hyper-local. Mention Happy Valley Road area in Lafayette, the Orinda hills, downtown WC corridor. This is the E-E-A-T section — proves Lamorinda actually works these specific neighborhoods.

outline.h2: How to budget for permits, drainage, and the 'unknowns'
outline.notes: Practical budgeting advice. Contra Costa permit costs. Drainage engineering when ground slopes. The contingency line — recommend 10-15% for unforeseen base prep.

outline.h2: How to vet a paver contractor's bid (red flags + green flags)
outline.notes: Pricing transparency, base prep depth specified in writing, warranty terms, ICPI certification, licensed/bonded check. Not salesy — written from the homeowner's perspective.

mustInclude: Specific neighborhoods: Happy Valley (Lafayette), the Orinda hills, downtown Walnut Creek
Clay soil constraint and how it affects base prep depth
Interlocking paver structural advantage over slab concrete on moving ground
ICPI (Interlocking Concrete Pavement Institute) certification mention
Real cost per sq ft ranges, not just project totals
Permit requirements vary by jurisdiction (Lafayette, Orinda, Moraga each)
mustAvoid: Generic 'paver driveways are beautiful and durable' filler
Vague phrases like 'the price depends on many factors' without naming them
Stock contractor language ('we pride ourselves on...', 'industry-leading')
Promising specific prices without ranges or conditions
cta: Tell the reader: if you want a real number for your specific property, request a free on-site estimate. Lamorinda will walk the lot, measure access constraints, evaluate the existing base, and send a fixed-price proposal in writing within 48 hours.
